_doc: RADE manifest (contract: rhope-ops/RADE schemas/rade-manifest.schema.json). Built by the RADE engine through scripts/build_paste_bundles.py (a pinned shim, see scripts/rade.lock.json). Each bundle is one round: a self-contained PowerShell text the PFM copies from its raw page and pastes into Windows PowerShell ISE (F5). It writes the files, then opens RADE, the Redacted Application Deployment Engine (a window; text prompts if no window can open): steps run one by one with a live log and PASS/FAIL counts, then one results folder (Rounds\\<round>: a report file plus copies of the PDFs, to attach to one e-mail; zips do not cross the boundary) and a summary for the clipboard. It runs only the steps inside it (PFM 3A). A step's "default" may be {passed, paths}: the step is ticked only when those files changed since the round that passed it; after a round passes it, set passed to the new hash (PFM 14 Nov 26). Never hand-edit scripts/gov/paste/*.ps1: change this file or the sources and rebuild. A step may list "needs" (check ids in the engine's $checkDefs) and "estimate" (minutes, used until a real run time exists). "apps" is the embedded catalog the Choose screen lists (name, plain-English summary, step names); without it, one application has every step. A guide step may set "doneText" (its Done button) and "doneLog" (the log line on Done).

bundles.title: Round R25: clean install from zero on the test site. After the old lists, flows and solutions are deleted by hand, RADE checks that the site is clean, builds the 12 lists by PnP (no provisioning flow), sets up the site, and the slice 1 flows are imported and tested on the new lists. First round on RADE engine-v6: questions are answered in the window

steps.name: T20 Clean the site by hand r1
steps.note: You confirm that the old test objects are deleted (the task "Clean the test site" on the bookmark page). The next step checks the site. About 1 minute (estimate).
steps.url_source: Microsoft Learn, Power Automate US Government (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/us-govt): DoD maker portal; editable in the window, remembered in Config (agent value, PFM to confirm in R13)
guide: 1. Before this round, do the task "Clean the test site" on the bookmark page (8 steps: solutions, flows, lists, the library, result files).
2. If it is done: select "Done: site is clean" and answer one question about Power Automate.
If it is not done: select "It failed", close RADE, do the task, then run the round again.

answers.prompt: Are all 90-161.Z solutions and flows deleted in Power Automate?

steps.name: T20 Clean site check r1
steps.note: Signs in (CAC) and reads only. Passes when the site has no PFM list, no 90-161.Z library, no 90161Z result file and no probe test group. Changes nothing. About 1 minute (estimate).
after: T20 Clean the site by hand r1
steps.help: Delete what the FAIL lines name (task "Clean the test site"), then run the round again.

steps.name: T20 Build the 12 lists r1
steps.note: Creates the 12 PFM lists with their columns, views, 88 seed rows, titles, indexes and edit-own-rows, then checks each list. It adds only; a second run skips what is there. About 5 minutes (estimate).
steps.help: Send the results as they are. The step can be run again: it skips what is there.

makes.name: the 12 PFM lists (PFM Offices to PFM Reviews)

steps.name: T16 Site setup r11
steps.note: Makes the 90-161.Z library again and uploads the seals from T07, checks the time zone, the header logo and edit-own-rows, and counts the lists and rows. About 4 minutes (estimate).
steps.help: Send the results as they are; each FAIL line names its own fix.

steps.name: T18 Import the slice 1 flows r5
steps.note: You import the 90-161.Z flows solution into the clean environment and answer 2 questions in this window. Value 3 (shared mailbox) stays empty in this round. About 7 minutes (estimate).
steps.url_source: Microsoft Learn, Power Automate US Government (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/us-govt): DoD maker portal; editable in the window, remembered in Config (agent value, PFM to confirm in R13)
guide: 1. Select "Open in browser". Power Automate opens; sign in with your CAC if asked.
2. Select Solutions (under More if it is not shown), then Import solution > Browse.
3. In the File name box, press Ctrl+V (the file path is on the clipboard), select Open, then Next.
4. Connections: for SharePoint and for Office 365 Outlook, select your existing connection.
5. Environment variables: find the 4 labels that start with 1 to 4. They can be in any order on the page; remember the order you see.
6. "1 Site URL": paste the test site address. "2 Alert e-mail": your own work e-mail address.
7. "3 Shared mailbox": leave it EMPTY in this round (it tests which mailbox sends). "4 Test mode" must read Yes. Keep all other values.
8. Select Import and wait for "Successfully imported" (1 to 3 minutes, estimate).
9. Open the solution "90-161.Z flows". F05 and F06 must read On and F03 Off; if one differs, change it.
10. Return to RADE, select "Done: imported" and answer the 2 questions.
If the import fails: select "Download log file" (any folder), type the first line of the red error (no names or site address) below, then select "It failed".
steps.help: Send the results as they are; the next step reads the import log if you downloaded it.

answers.prompt: In which order did the page show the 4 numbered values? Type the numbers, for example 1 3 4 2.
What did "4 Test mode" read before you changed anything?

steps.name: T17 Import log reader r2
steps.note: Runs only if the import failed: copies the error rows of an import log saved in the last 3 hours to T17, addresses masked. Otherwise it reports SKIPPED.

steps.name: T18 Slice 1 test, part 1 r4
steps.note: Signs in (CAC). Creates three fake publications at step 6 on the new lists and checks F05: rows for A only, F after its title fix, one removed row added back. Sets two rows past due for F03.
after: T18 Import the slice 1 flows r5
steps.help: Send the results as they are. A FAIL here on new lists is a finding about the lists or the flows.

steps.name: T18 Failure e-mail and Resubmit r1
steps.note: You check that F05 e-mailed you about the forced failure, then select Resubmit on that failed run. About 4 minutes (estimate).
steps.url_source: Microsoft Learn, Power Automate US Government (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/us-govt): DoD maker portal; editable in the window, remembered in Config (agent value, PFM to confirm in R13)
guide: 1. In Outlook, find the e-mail "90-161.Z flow failed: F05" (it arrived in part 1). It names the step "Test hook forced failure". Do not reply.
2. Select "Open in browser" and open Solutions > "90-161.Z flows" > "90161Z F05 Endorsement Routing r2".
3. Under 28-day run history, select the run marked Failed (the time in the e-mail).
4. Select Resubmit at the top of the run. Wait until the new run shows Succeeded (under 1 minute, estimate).
5. Return to RADE and select "Done: resubmitted".
If no failure e-mail arrived, or there is no failed run: type what you see (no names or site address) in the box below, then select "It failed".

steps.name: T18 Run F03 once r5
steps.note: You run F03 once by hand. In test mode its e-mails go only to you; in this round your own mailbox sends them. The last step asks where the e-mail arrived. About 3 minutes (estimate).
steps.url_source: Microsoft Learn, Power Automate US Government (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/us-govt): DoD maker portal; editable in the window, remembered in Config (agent value, PFM to confirm in R13)
guide: 1. Safety check: if Test mode did not read Yes at import, select "Skip": F03 would e-mail real endorsers.
2. Select "Open in browser" and open Solutions > "90-161.Z flows".
3. Open "90161Z F03 Suspense Reminders r5" and select Test > Manually > Test, then Run flow.
4. Wait until the run ends (under 1 minute, estimate). Read only the status at the top of the run: "Succeeded" or "Failed".
5. Grey (skipped) steps are normal: the last 3 steps, one of the two send steps, and most rows of the loop send nothing.
6. If the status is Succeeded: return to RADE and select "Done: F03 ran". The last step of the round asks about the e-mail.
If the status is Failed: type the name of the first step with a red mark and the first line of its error (no names or site address), then select "It failed".

steps.name: T18 Slice 1 test, part 2 r4
steps.note: Checks: Resubmit made no duplicates; F03 suspense and one escalation; F06 hold, resume and cancel; Legal rows and step 7. Line j2 names the mailbox that sent the e-mail. Removes all test rows.
steps.help: Send the results as they are. The test rows stay on the site for review when a check fails.

steps.name: T18 Find the test e-mail r1
steps.note: You look for the F03 test e-mail and answer one question in this window. This closes a fault of 4 rounds: the e-mail was logged but never found. About 2 minutes (estimate).
guide: 1. In Outlook, search All Mailboxes for a subject that starts with "[TEST] Escalation", received today.
2. Look in this order: Inbox, Junk E-mail, then Sent Items.
3. Select "Done: I looked" and answer where you found it.
If Outlook does not open: select "It failed" and type what you see (no names or addresses).

answers.prompt: Where is the e-mail "[TEST] Escalation" from this round?

steps.name: RADE Window questions r1
steps.note: You answer 4 short questions about this window: restore after minimize, button borders, alignment. This replaces notes in the e-mail. About 2 minutes (estimate).
guide: 1. Minimize this window now (the button with the line, top right).
2. Select RADE on the taskbar. The window must come back at its size, not as a full screen.
3. Select "Done: I looked" and answer the 4 questions.
If the window does not come back: maximize it to go on, select "Done: I looked" and answer No to the first question.

answers.prompt: Did the window come back from the taskbar after you minimized it?
Did every button and choice show only a thin border? A black or gray outline around one counts as No.
Were the lines and buttons aligned on every card?
Did anything look wrong? Name the card and the part. Do not type names or addresses.
